# Rachel Lynde

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** housewife  <sub>[v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mrs. Rachel  <sub>[v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Mrs. Rachel Lynde sits regularly at her kitchen window keeping watch over the Avonlea main road.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P0](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0000), [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001)_

## Personality

Mrs. Rachel is a capable, hardworking, and outspoken woman who prides herself on always speaking her mind. Though she can be officious, critical, and given to nagging, she possesses a kindly heart and is quick to acknowledge her own mistakes. She is an active church participant, a passionate politician, and loves giving advice to others.

_Sources: [v1 c1 P1](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0001), [v1 c1 P24](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0024), [v1 c9 P14](../source/v01-c09.md#nw-v01-c09-p0014), [v1 c10 P33](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0033), [v1 c15 P89](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0089), [v1 c18 P1](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0001), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c31 P7](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0007)_

## History

Mrs. Rachel Lynde lives in Lynde's Hollow where her window overlooks the main road to Avonlea. She has raised ten children and buried two, while managing her house, running the Sewing Circle, helping with Sunday school, and supporting the Church Aid Society and Foreign Missions Auxiliary. Upon discovering that the Cuthberts plan to adopt a boy, she visits Green Gables and later meets Anne Shirley, whom she severely criticizes for her looks, prompting a furious outburst from Anne. After Anne apologizes, Mrs. Rachel forgives her and warms to her, later making her a dress on Matthew's behalf. As a devoted Liberal, Mrs. Rachel attends a major political rally in Charlottetown alongside Marilla Cuthbert and her husband Thomas. She also participates in an exhibition where her homemade butter and cheese win first prize, though she refuses to watch the horse racing on moral grounds. When Anne excels at Queen's and earns her teaching license, Mrs. Rachel eventually admits her initial misjudgment of the girl, while remaining skeptical of higher education for women.
